battle.name: 薩英戰爭
battle.brief: 一八六三年八月十五日，英國海軍七艦以阿姆斯特朗後膛炮砲擊鹿兒島灣，逼薩摩藩就生麥事件的賠償與究辦讓步。薩摩岸砲在颱風中先發制人，午後炮戰約兩小時，英軍傷亡不輕卻未登陸奪砲，兩天後撤退。卡面這件法國一八四〇年式的雷管步槍，正是當時薩摩藩洋槍隊所用的那一代歐製步槍。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的兩方，一方是英國，一方是日本薩摩藩，背後各有一套不同的國家機器。英方由大不列顛及愛爾蘭聯合王國的皇家海軍執行任務：遠征隊由東印度艦隊司令奧古斯都·庫帕中將率領，旗艦是木殼蒸汽巡防艦尤里亞勒斯號，英國駐日代理公使約翰·尼爾隨艦坐鎮，談判與武力都由他與艦隊一併推進。艦隊共七艘蒸汽軍艦，除旗艦外尚有珍珠號、珀爾修斯號、阿格斯號、科凱特號、賽馬號，以及炮艦哈沃克號；編制上是一支不打算登陸、只用艦砲執行條約的武力，英方的要求只有三項：薩摩藩道歉、交出涉事者受審、賠償二萬五千英鎊。薩摩方的權力中心在藩主島津茂久（事後改名島津忠義）與攝政島津久光手裡，鹿兒島城下町的守備由藩士與町人編成的警護與砲隊擔當，藩內早已設有洋槍隊與洋艦隊，一八六〇年代初落成的集成館兵工廠負責自鑄砲身與鍛造彈藥，薩摩藩是幕末最主張開國的藩之一。第三方是德川幕府：一八六三年八月四日幕府致函英方請求延緩出動，又表示打算派一艘軍艦同行，卻在薩摩藩被扣押商船之後先行退讓，最終代薩摩藩墊付賠款，明治維新後再也追不回。幕府層面的壓力則來自英法兩國：一八六三年七月二日，幕府代表登上法國旗艦塞米拉米斯號，與英法代表談判並當場支付賠償。
countriesEn: The two sides were Great Britain and the Satsuma Domain of Japan, each backed by a different state machinery. The British side was the Royal Navy of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland: the expedition was led by Admiral Augustus Kuper, commander of the East Indies Station, with the wooden-hulled screw frigate HMS Euryalus as his flagship, and the British chargé d'affaires to Japan, Edward St. John Neale, travelling on board the flagship so that negotiation and force advanced together. The squadron numbered seven steam warships — besides the flagship, the Pearl, Perseus, Argus, Coquette and Racehorse, together with the gunboat Havock. In organisation it was a force that never intended to land, and that meant to enforce the treaty with the guns of the fleet alone. The British demands came down to three items: an apology from Satsuma, the surrender of those responsible for trial, and an indemnity of 25,000 pounds sterling. On the Satsuma side the centre of power lay with the daimyo Shimazu Tadayoshi, later known as Shimazu Tadashige, and with the regent Shimazu Hisamitsu, who together handled the defence of the town of Kagoshima through the guard and the artillery companies drawn from the domain samurai and the town militia. The domain already had a Western-style rifle corps and a Western-style flotilla, and the Shugokan ordnance works, completed in the early 1860s, cast gun barrels and forged ammunition on site; Satsuma was among the strongest advocates of opening Japan to the outside. The third party was the Tokugawa shogunate: on 4 August 1863 it wrote to the British asking for a delay, and said it intended to send a warship to join the expedition, but it backed down once the British seized Satsuma merchantmen, and it ended by advancing the indemnity on the domain's behalf, a sum never recovered after the Meiji government came to power. At the shogunate level the pressure came from Britain and France together: on 2 July 1863 the shogunate's delegates boarded the French frigate Semiramis, negotiated with the British and French representatives, and paid the indemnity there and then.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩邊。英方最先要說的是代理公使約翰·尼爾：生麥事件之後，他先向幕府索取十萬英鎊，再把要求壓到薩摩藩身上，聲明限期答覆、否則用兵，最後全程隨艦，坐鎮尤里亞勒斯號。海軍方面由奧古斯都·庫帕中將指揮這支七艦遠征隊，下令扣押商船、准許還擊，也在三日後下令撤退。尤里亞勒斯號艦長約翰·詹姆斯·史蒂文·約斯林與副官愛德華·威爾莫特同日被同一發砲彈削去首級，該艦另有八名艦員陣亡，紀念牌後來立於橫濱英國領事館舊址。薩摩方面，藩主島津茂久與攝政島津久光是真正的決策者，最後兩人選擇接受英方要求；主戰一派則有奈良原喜左衛門、海江田信義與家老大山巖等人，奈良原與海江田正是生麥事件的行凶者，並在開戰前夕策劃以偽裝成西瓜商人的方式登上英艦行刺。幕府方的翻譯福澤諭吉同樣關鍵：他的傳譯使英方以為薩摩要處分藩主，薩摩卻以為英方只要求處罰行凶的武士，雙方對責任的認知自此錯開。據薩摩方面的記錄，東鄉平八郎當時以砲手身分參與偽裝行動，在鹿兒島砲台服役；大山巖所著的《元帥公爵大山巖》則是薩摩方面陣亡、負傷與火炮損失數字的來源。
peopleEn: The decisive figures fall on either side of the line. On the British side the first name is the chargé d'affaires Edward St. John Neale: after the Namamugi incident he first demanded 100,000 pounds from the shogunate, then transferred the demand to the Satsuma Domain, declared that he would use force if his terms were not met in time, and finally sailed with the squadron, sitting on the Euryalus. At sea the expedition of seven ships was under Admiral Augustus Kuper, who ordered the seizure of the merchantmen, authorised the return fire, and three days later ordered the squadron away. The captain of the Euryalus, John James Steven Josling, and her executive officer, Commander Edward Wilmot, were both decapitated by the same cannonball on the same day, and eight other members of the crew were killed; a memorial to them was later set up in the former British consular building at Yokohama. On the Satsuma side the real decision-makers were the daimyo Shimazu Tadayoshi and the regent Shimazu Hisamitsu, who between them chose to accept the British terms. The party favouring a fight included Narahara Kizaemon, Kaieda Nobuyoshi and the senior retainer Oyama Iwao; Narahara and Kaieda were the men who had killed Richardson at Namamugi, and before hostilities opened they planned to gain access to a British ship disguised as melon merchants, in order to strike. The shogunate's interpreter Fukuzawa Yukichi mattered just as much: his rendering left the British convinced that Satsuma intended to hand over the daimyo himself, while Satsuma understood that the British merely wanted the murderers punished, and from that moment the two sides read responsibility in incompatible ways. According to the Satsuma accounts, Togo Heihachiro took part in the disguised operation at this time and served as a gunner on the Kagoshima batteries; the casualty and gun-loss figures quoted on the Satsuma side come from Oyama Iwao's own account, the Marshal Duke Oyama Iwao.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是法國在一八四〇年前後定裝的雷管線膛步槍。它以銅製雷管取代燧石，槍機改為後膛機匣，射擊時不必再靠火石敲擊與火繩點燃；槍口以紙包定裝藥一次送入火藥與彈丸，每人攜帶八十發，槍身下緣裝刺刀，槍口徑約十四點七毫米，初速約每秒四百公尺，最大射程一般記為千公尺上下，但戰場上能倚賴的射距多在二百公尺左右。雷管底火最大的好處是不怕潮濕與海霧，只要銅管與火藥沒受潮，槍就能打得響，這正是幕末薩摩藩在雨夜與海霧中倚賴的性能。在薩摩藩的體系裡，這一類歐製雷管步槍的位置在洋槍隊。薩摩藩是幕末購置西洋軍火最積極的藩之一，洋槍隊以法式操典操練，所用步槍多自長崎與上海的外商渠道購入，一八六〇年代初落成的集成館兵工廠則負責自鑄砲身、鍛造彈藥與試射；火炮一面則以江戶時代自鑄的大口徑青銅砲為主，例如一八四九年薩摩自鑄、口徑二百九十毫米、砲身長四千二百二十毫米的一五〇磅砲，安置在天保山砲台。英方對應的裝備屬另一個技術世代：尤里亞勒斯號備有三十五門主炮與約十六門卡隆砲，其中十七門是阿姆斯特朗後膛炮，另有前裝滑膛炮，艦上水手則用一八五三年恩菲尔德等英國制式雷管步槍。雙方的差距不在步槍，而在岸防大砲：薩摩的青銅砲射速低、射程短，又沒有後膛與雷管這類改良可用。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the French percussion rifle as standardised around 1840. It replaces the flint with a copper percussion cap and moves the lock to a breech block, so that firing no longer depends on striking steel and burning a match. A paper cartridge carries powder and ball in one charge, eighty of which a soldier carried; a bayonet was socketed under the barrel, the bore was about 14.7 millimetres, the muzzle velocity ran to roughly 400 metres per second, and maximum range is generally given as around a thousand metres, though the range a soldier could actually depend on in the field was nearer two hundred. The great virtue of the percussion cap is that it does not mind damp and sea fog: as long as the cap and the powder have stayed dry, the gun will go off, and that reliability in wet night weather was exactly what a Satsuma detachment came to lean on. Within the Satsuma system, rifles of this European percussion type stood in the Western-style rifle corps. Satsuma was among the most active domains of the late Bakumatsu in buying foreign arms; the rifle corps was drilled on French manual methods, and the muskets were largely bought through foreign traders at Nagasaki and Shanghai, while the Shugokan ordnance works, finished in the early 1860s, cast gun barrels, forged ammunition and carried out proof firing. On the artillery side the coastal batteries relied mainly on large-calibre bronze guns cast in the Edo period, among them a 150-pounder cast by Satsuma in 1849, of 290 millimetre calibre and 4,220 millimetres in barrel length, mounted on Fort Tenpozan. The British equipment belonged to a different technological generation: the Euryalus carried thirty-five main guns and some sixteen carronades, of which seventeen were Armstrong breech-loaders, together with muzzle-loading smoothbore guns, while the ship's boats' crews used British service percussion muskets such as the 1853 Enfield. The gap between the two sides did not lie in the muskets at all; it lay in the heavy coastal guns, for Satsuma's bronze pieces were slow in rate of fire, short in range, and had no breech or percussion mechanism to improve them.
tactics: 開戰前一個月，雙方都在談判與備戰的縫隙裡準備對方。英方要求薩摩藩限期答覆，薩摩藩一面以使節拖延，一面策劃以偽裝使者的方式登上英艦，圖先發制人；一八六三年八月十四日最後通牒送達後，薩摩藩主戰一派決定先動手。八月十五日中午，薩摩藩岸防砲在颱風與驟雨中先發制人。作戰地理很簡單：英艦隊錨泊在鹿兒島灣西側，薩摩的砲台分佈在金剛山、城山、天保山等高地與沿岸，居高臨下交叉射擊；薩摩藩還特意等颱風來時才開火，想借雨幕與海面搖晃壓低英方命中率。英方吃了虧：艦隊並未為持久戰作準備，火砲瞄準與裝填程序都嫌草率，加上颱風中船身搖擺，約兩小時的炮戰裡，包括艦長在內十餘人陣亡，近六十人受傷。英方的反應是典型的十九世紀海權砲艦外交：以百門艦炮的齊射壓制岸砲，同時摧毀城下町的集成館兵工廠一帶與三艘蒸汽船，使薩摩藩失去繼續造炮的工場；十六日再砲擊櫻島，十七日退出鹿兒島灣，全程不登陸、不奪取薩摩的火砲，把戰果控制在足以施壓而不足以羞辱對方的分寸上。就槍械而言，雷管步槍的射程拉長也改變了隊形：密集縱隊在稀疏而精準的火力下容易被打散，防守一方只能靠散兵線與地形遮蔽；反過來，暴雨中仍能擊發的雷管，讓砲台周圍的近射火力維持了密度，也讓守軍在視線不良時仍能維持射擊。
tacticsEn: During the month before hostilities, both sides prepared for the other in the gaps between negotiation and mobilisation. The British demanded an answer within a fixed term; Satsuma stalled through envoys while planning to gain access to a British ship under the disguise of envoys, in order to strike first. When the final ultimatum arrived on 14 August 1863, the party favouring war in the domain decided to move first. At midday on 15 August the Satsuma shore batteries opened fire in a typhoon and sudden rain. The geography of the action was simple: the British squadron lay anchored on the western side of Kagoshima Bay, and the Satsuma batteries were distributed over the heights of Kinkoyama, Shiroyama and Tenpozan and along the shore, firing in crossfire from above. Satsuma had deliberately waited for the typhoon to open fire, hoping to depress British accuracy through the curtain of rain and the roll of the sea. The British paid for that: the squadron was not fitted out for a prolonged action, the gunnery was hurried and careless, and with the hulls rolling in the storm, some ten or more men were killed in the two hours of gunnery, including the captain, and nearly sixty wounded. The British reply was typical nineteenth-century naval gunboat diplomacy: a simultaneous salvo of about a hundred ship guns to silence the shore batteries, at the same time destroying the Shugokan ordnance works and the three steamers in the town, so that the domain lost the means of casting further guns; on the sixteenth they bombarded Sakurajima, and on the seventeenth they withdrew from Kagoshima Bay, never landing and never carrying off the Satsuma guns, keeping the result on a scale that could put pressure without humiliating. As far as the weapons go, the extended range of the percussion rifle also changed the shape of formations: close columns were easily broken up by sparse but accurate fire, and a defending side could rely only on skirmish lines and cover; in the other direction, a percussion cap that still fired in the rain let the close-in weapons around the batteries keep up their density and let the garrisons keep shooting when they could hardly see.
data: 時間線可以逐日排出來：一八六三年八月六日英艦隊自橫濱出發，八月十一日抵達鹿兒島灣，在城南約七公里的谷山近海錨泊；八月十二日進至城下町前之濱外海約一公里處；八月十三日薩摩藩在回覆中否認有責任；八月十四日英方下達最後通牒；八月十五日中午薩摩岸砲先射，十四時英方以約百門艦炮還擊，炮戰約兩小時；八月十六日十六時英方砲擊櫻島，十七日十六時離開鹿兒島灣返橫濱。火力方面：英方七艦之中，旗艦尤里亞勒斯號排水三千一百二十五噸，艦員五百一十五人，主炮三十五門外加卡隆砲約十六門，其中十七門為阿姆斯特朗後膛炮，隨艦攜煤二百三十噸、炮彈與火藥七十餘噸。薩摩方的岸防砲，英方估計逾八十門，另有前述一八四九年自鑄的一五〇磅砲；兵員方面雙方都沒有留下可靠的編制數字，可確定的是薩摩出動的是町民、藩士與臨時集合起來的砲隊。傷亡與損失：英方各項統計略有出入，概數是陣亡十三人、受傷五十九至六十九人，其中尤里亞勒斯號上陣亡十人；薩摩藩自稱陣亡五人、受傷九人，損失火砲八門、彈藥庫兩座；英方扣押並焚毀三艘蒸汽船（英方記為席爾·喬治·格雷號、康泰斯特號與英格蘭號，總值約二十萬英鎊，薩摩方面的記法則作白鳳丸、天佑丸與青鷹丸），另有五艘琉球商船在炮火中燒毀。賠款是二萬五千英鎊，折約六萬三千日本銀兩，由幕府代付；對照之下，幕府在生麥事件上向英方支付的十萬英鎊，約相當於幕府年收入的三分之一。
dataEn: The chronology can be set out day by day. On 6 August 1863 the British squadron sailed from Yokohama; on the eleventh it reached Kagoshima Bay and anchored off Tanayama, about seven kilometres south of the town; on the twelfth it moved to about a kilometre off Maehama in front of the town; on the thirteenth Satsuma replied denying any responsibility; on the fourteenth the British delivered their final ultimatum; at midday on the fifteenth the Satsuma shore batteries fired first and at two in the afternoon the British replied with about a hundred ship guns, the gunnery lasting some two hours; at four in the afternoon on the sixteenth the British bombarded Sakurajima, and at four in the afternoon on the seventeenth they left Kagoshima Bay for Yokohama. In material terms: of the seven British ships the flagship Euryalus displaced 3,125 tons, carried 515 men, mounted thirty-five main guns plus some sixteen carronades of which seventeen were Armstrong breech-loaders, and carried 230 tons of coal and more than seventy tons of shot and shell. The British reckoned the Satsuma shore batteries at upwards of eighty guns, in addition to the 150-pounder cast in 1849; on the numbers of men no reliable establishment figures survive on either side, but what is certain is that Satsuma put into the line the town militia, domain samurai and gun crews hastily gathered. Casualties and losses: the British figures differ slightly between sources, roughly thirteen killed and fifty-nine to sixty-nine wounded, of whom ten were killed on the Euryalus alone; Satsuma claimed five killed and nine wounded, with eight guns and two powder magazines lost; the British seized and then burned three steamers, recorded on the British side as the Sir George Grey, the Contest and the England, with an aggregate value of some 200,000 pounds, while the Satsuma accounts name them the Hakuhomaru, Tennjomaru and Seiyomaru, and a further five Ryukyuan trading junks were burned in the gunnery. The indemnity was 25,000 pounds sterling, equivalent to about 63,000 silver ryo, advanced by the shogunate; by contrast the 100,000 pounds the shogunate paid the British over the Namamugi incident was about a third of the shogunate's annual revenue.
cause: 這場戰爭的起因，要從一八六二年九月十四日的生麥事件說起。英國商人查爾斯·李諾克斯·理查森與另外三名同行者在神奈川縣生麥村旅行，事前已被提醒當日島津久光的行列將通過東海道，卻仍騎馬不讓道，衝進隊伍之中；薩摩藩家臣奈良原喜左衛門、海江田信義等依切捨御免將其砍殺，事後驗屍記錄十處致命傷，同行的克拉克與馬歇爾重傷。英方認為這違反了治外法權下英人的豁免，幕府與薩摩藩都必須負責。幕府的反應快而軟：代理公使尼爾索取十萬英鎊並揚言砲擊江戶，幕府在恐懼下於一八六三年七月二日登上法國旗艦塞米拉米斯號，向英法道歉並當場付款，暫時了結了幕府這一環。麻煩留給了薩摩藩：尼爾要求薩摩藩道歉、賠償二萬五千英鎊，並拘捕行凶者受審；薩摩藩的答覆是生麥事件並無責任可言，理由是切捨御免本就是武士對無禮者的制裁，該受處分的行凶武士不必牽連藩主。這正是導火線。薩摩藩同時還在英方眼中欠著另一筆帳：據當時的記錄，一八六二年九月一艘英國商船在鹿兒島灣外遭薩摩砲台射擊、船上旗幟被擊落，此案索賠也未了結。兩案相加，英國政府批准動用武力，於是有了八月六日自橫濱出發的七艦遠征。
causeEn: The origins of this war run back to the Namamugi incident of 14 September 1862. The British merchant Charles Lennox Richardson and three companions were travelling through the village of Namamugi in Kanagawa Prefecture; they had already been warned that the procession of Shimazu Hisamitsu would pass that day along the Tokaido, yet they rode on without dismounting and pushed into the column. The Satsuma retainers Narahara Kizaemon and Kaieda Nobuyoshi cut him down under the right of kiri-sute-gomen; the post-mortem recorded ten mortal wounds, and his companions Clark and Marshall were grievously hurt. The British held that this violated the immunity of British subjects under the extraterritoriality treaties, and that both the shogunate and the Satsuma Domain bore responsibility. The shogunate reacted quickly but weakly: the chargé d'affaires Neale demanded 100,000 pounds and threatened to bombard Edo, and the shogunate, frightened, boarded the French frigate Semiramis on 2 July 1863, apologised to Britain and France and paid on the spot, disposing of its own part of the affair. What remained was Satsuma's problem. Neale demanded an apology, 25,000 pounds and the arrest and trial of the murderers; Satsuma's answer was that it had no responsibility in the matter, on the ground that kiri-sute-gomen was the sanction a warrior owed to an impolite offender, and that the individual who had struck should be punished without dragging in the daimyo. That was the fuse. Satsuma was also, in British eyes, still in debt over a second matter: according to the records of the time, a British merchant vessel was fired on by Satsuma shore batteries outside Kagoshima Bay in September 1862 and had her ensign shot away, and that claim was likewise unresolved. Taken together the two cases persuaded the British government to authorise force, and so the seven-ship expedition left Yokohama on 6 August.
impact: 這場戰爭對日本的影響，遠大於它在戰術上的規模。薩摩藩在英方最後通牒與藩內主和派的壓力下屈服，於一八六三年十一月十五日簽約，支付二萬五千英鎊；款項由幕府代付，而明治政府成立後再也沒有向薩摩藩追討，幕府手上多了一筆永久的呆帳。薩摩藩由此明白，靠江戶時代的青銅砲與舊式火繩槍，無法與蒸汽戰艦和後膛炮對抗，攘夷在本藩已經走不通。另一面則是轉機：英國同意向薩摩藩出售蒸汽軍艦，薩摩藩的西化從此有了資金與艦隊，洋式海軍、兵制與兵學校在藩內迅速鋪開；一八六八年戊辰戰爭爆發時，薩摩藩與英國站在同一邊，鳥羽伏見的戰鬥中英艦曾炮擊京都側的軍隊，而薩摩藩也由此看清幕府無法再依靠，作為倒幕的決定性一環，薩摩藩站到了打倒幕府的一邊。在國際層面，這是日本第一次以藩的名義單獨向西方國家支付巨額賠償，也是日本各藩第一次在同一場衝突裡直接看見近代火力與傳統防禦的差距。尊王攘夷的旗號並未因此消失，但它在薩摩藩內部失去了說服力。技術面上，阿姆斯特朗後膛炮首次用於對岸攻擊，岸防要塞在蒸汽艦隊面前失去優勢的印象，也刺激了後來的海岸砲台近代化。
impactEn: The effect of this war on Japan was far larger than its tactical scale. Satsuma yielded to the British ultimatum and to the pressure of its own party for peace, signing on 15 November 1863 and paying 25,000 pounds sterling; the money was advanced by the shogunate and was never claimed back from the domain once the Meiji government was in power, leaving a permanent bad debt on the shogunate's books. Satsuma learned that Edo-period bronze guns and old matchlock muskets could not stand against steam warships and breech-loading artillery, and that the expulsion of the foreigners was no longer workable within the domain. The other side of the same coin was an opening: Britain agreed to sell steam warships to Satsuma, and the domain's westernisation acquired money and a fleet, with a Western-style navy, service system and military academy spreading quickly inside it. When the Boshin War broke out in 1868, Satsuma stood on the same side as Britain; in the fighting at Toba-Fushimi British ships shelled troops on the Kyoto side, and Satsuma likewise saw that the shogunate could no longer be relied upon, which made its turn to the overthrow of the shogunate the decisive one. At the international level this was the first time a Japanese domain paid a large indemnity to a Western power in its own name, and the first occasion on which the domains of Japan had seen, in a single engagement, the gap between modern firepower and traditional defence. The banner of sonno joi did not disappear because of it, but it lost its persuasive force inside Satsuma. On the technical side, the Armstrong breech-loader was used for the first time against shore targets; the impression that coastal fortresses had been rendered obsolete by steam squadrons pushed the later modernisation of shore batteries.
result: 結果要分軍事與政治兩層看。軍事上，英方以艦砲壓制了薩摩的岸防砲，摧毀集成館兵工廠一帶與三艘蒸汽船，使薩摩藩一時失去造炮與航運的骨幹；英軍自身付出十餘人陣亡、近六十人受傷的代價，數艘軍艦受創。但英國沒有登陸，沒有奪取薩摩的火砲，也沒有佔領城下町，這些都是英方刻意的克制，目的是讓談判可以繼續。政治上，雙方都能宣稱勝利：薩摩藩以雙方傷亡數字比較，宣布抵禦住了外國艦隊；英國則得到實質結果，薩摩藩承認責任並支付賠償。一八六三年十一月十五日英薩講和，薩摩藩付出二萬五千英鎊，英方未取得行凶者受審的結果，卻換來了向薩摩藩出售蒸汽軍艦的權利。戰後的薩摩藩著手重建砲台、擴充洋槍隊與蒸氣艦隊，砲兵開始引用英法兩國的操典與射擊教程；一八六四年英國還以海陸聯合部隊參與第二次長州征討，與薩摩藩並肩作戰。對日本而言，這場戰爭的終點不是勝負，而是薩摩藩從攘夷轉向開國的那一刻。
resultEn: The outcome has to be read on two levels, military and political. Militarily the British silenced the Satsuma shore batteries with ship guns, destroyed the Shugokan ordnance works and the three steamers, and left the domain for the time without the backbone of its gun-casting and its shipping; the British themselves paid with more than ten men killed and nearly sixty wounded, and several of their ships were damaged. But Britain did not land, did not carry off the Satsuma guns and did not occupy the town; these were deliberate acts of restraint, meant to keep the negotiation alive. Politically, both sides could claim a victory: Satsuma compared the casualty figures and announced that it had withstood the foreign squadron, while Britain obtained the substance, namely Satsuma's admission of responsibility and the payment of the indemnity. Peace was signed on 15 November 1863: Satsuma paid 25,000 pounds sterling, the British did not obtain the trial of the murderers, and in exchange secured the right to sell steam warships to the domain. After the war Satsuma set about rebuilding its batteries and expanding its Western-style rifle corps and steam flotilla, its artillery beginning to quote British and French manuals and shooting instruction; in 1864 Britain took part in the Second Chōshū Expedition with a combined naval and military force, fighting alongside Satsuma. For Japan the end point of this war was not a verdict of win or loss but the moment at which Satsuma turned from the expulsion of the foreigners to the opening of the country.
